problem_statement: The facebook/regenerator docs site is a static browser page at docs/index.html with an interactive transformer sandbox (Input -> transformed Output) and a Regenerator/Traceur comparison toggle, plus local yield-ahead image assets. The site carries a shared masthead navigation rendered from a shared nav-links registry (docs/nav-links.js) mounted by docs/site-nav.js, with a nav-link class on each anchor, and a shared footer. The docs do not yet document WHICH ES6 generator patterns the transform actually rewrites. Add a new cross-page Transform gallery at /docs/gallery.html: a catalogue of the real generator/yield patterns regenerator lowers to ES5, shown as a responsive grid of pattern cards (each with a local yield-ahead icon, an h3 headline, a short note, and a code snippet), fronted by a category filter (All patterns / Generators / Delegation / Async / Iteration) that filters the grid and updates a live count readout of the form 'Showing N of 6 . Label'. Register a 'Transform gallery' entry in the shared nav-links registry so the nav-link renders on both the docs home and the gallery page. Wire the filter in docs/gallery-filter.js so clicking a category hides the non-matching cards and recomputes the readout from the visible cards. Do not convert the docs into a new app or build system, remove the transformer sandbox or the Regenerator/Traceur comparison toggle, or replace the local yield-ahead assets; the gallery must conform to the existing static docs design system (sans-serif type, simple bordered cards, compact content column) and to the shared cross-page navigation.
required_content: Add a new Transform gallery page at /docs/gallery.html built from a responsive pattern-card grid: at least six figure.pattern-card cards, each with a local yield-ahead icon image, an h3 headline, a short note, and a code snippet.

Add a category filter above the grid (five .gallery-tab buttons: All patterns, Generators, Delegation, Async, Iteration) and a live #gallery-readout that reads 'Showing 6 of 6 . All patterns' initially and recomputes to match the visible cards when a category is selected.

Wire docs/gallery-filter.js so clicking a category tab filters the grid to matching data-category cards, marks the active tab, and updates the readout; clicking 'Delegation' must show 'Showing 1 of 6 . Delegation'.

Register a 'Transform gallery' entry in the shared nav-links registry (docs/nav-links.js) so an <a class="nav-link"> for Transform gallery renders in the shared masthead navigation on both the docs home and the gallery page.

Keep the page heading 'Every generator pattern regenerator rewrites to ES5.' and the six card headlines Basic generator function, Two-way yield value, Delegated yield*, Async generator, Await inside a generator, and for-of over a generator.

Preserve the original docs home content and behavior: the 'get serious about ES6 generator functions' heading, the Regenerator/Traceur comparison toggle, the Input:/Output: sandbox, and the local docs assets; do not add a standalone off-system Cheatsheet page.
The Transform gallery must have no horizontal overflow on desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile; the filter tab row must wrap and the pattern-card grid must stack cleanly on mobile.
state_constraints: desktop_home / mobile_home / tablet_home capture the original Regenerator docs home now carrying the shared masthead nav (with the registered Transform gallery nav-link) and footer.

desktop_gallery / mobile_gallery / tablet_gallery capture the new Transform gallery page: the shared nav with the Transform gallery nav-link, the category filter with its live readout, the six-card responsive pattern grid, and the shared footer.

desktop_gallery_filter clicks the 'Delegation' category tab on the gallery page and verifies the grid filters to the delegation card and the readout updates to 'Showing 1 of 6 . Delegation', changed from the 'Showing 6 of 6 . All patterns' pre-click state.

Source inspection confirms the shared nav is rendered from docs/nav-links.js mounted by docs/site-nav.js on every page, and the filter behavior lives in docs/gallery-filter.js, so a registered cross-page nav link and a wired filter are machine-detectable.
design_constraints: Keep the implementation in the existing static docs architecture; do not introduce React, a build system, a new package manager, or external asset hosting.
Reuse the shared masthead nav and footer and the shared nav-links registry rather than inventing a one-off navigation.
The Transform gallery is a repo-grounded docs feature that catalogues the generator patterns regenerator rewrites, with a category filter and live count, not a marketing hero or a separate app.
Use only repo-local yield-ahead assets for the pattern-card icons; do not add generic stock images or an off-system Cheatsheet surface.
Desktop uses a multi-column pattern-card grid and a wrapping tab row; 390px mobile stacks the cards to one column and wraps the tab row without horizontal overflow.

change_completion: The Transform gallery renders the six pattern cards, the page heading, the yield-ahead icons, and the code snippets.
The category filter and its live readout are present, and the Transform gallery nav-link is registered and renders on both the docs home and the gallery page.
design_consistency: The Transform gallery matches the static docs sans-serif, simple-bordered-card visual system.
The gallery is a repo-grounded docs feature built from the shared nav/footer chrome, not an off-system one-off Cheatsheet.
regression: The original generator explanation, Regenerator/Traceur comparison toggle, Input/Output sandbox, and local docs assets remain intact.
A correct patch is an additive HTML/CSS/JS/registry change, not a framework rewrite or asset swap.
responsive: The Transform gallery has no horizontal overflow on desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile.
The filter tab row wraps and the pattern-card grid stacks to a single column on 390px mobile without clipping cards.

scoring_notes: A correct patch adds a repo-grounded Transform gallery docs page built from a responsive pattern-card grid and a working category filter with a live count readout, and registers a 'Transform gallery' entry in the shared nav registry so the nav-link renders cross-page. A layout-only regression (fixed-width nowrap tab row overflow, rigid grid overrun, or a dropped nav-link) fails no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, and dom_assertions but not the interaction gate; a smart-wrong filter (frozen count, unfiltered grid) additionally fails the interaction gate. Shipping a standalone off-system Cheatsheet, omitting the pattern grid, or failing to register the nav-link should fail completion, visible, forbidden, and dom checks.
author_notes: Hardened to a product-grade L4 content_asset_continuity Consistency (add/cross_page) task on the facebook/regenerator static docs site. The native lever is a Transform gallery docs page (docs/gallery.html): a responsive pattern-card grid of the real ES6 generator/yield patterns the regenerator transform rewrites to ES5 (basic generator, two-way yield, delegated yield*, async generator, await-in-generator, for-of), fronted by a category filter (All patterns / Generators / Delegation / Async / Iteration) with a live 'Showing N of 6 . Label' count readout wired in docs/gallery-filter.js. A 'Transform gallery' entry is registered in the shared nav-links registry (docs/nav-links.js) so the cross-page nav-link renders on both the docs home and the gallery page. Reference passes all four gates. The baseline ships the pre-polish gallery CSS (a fixed-width nowrap tab row that overflows on mobile/tablet and a rigid fixed-width four-column grid that overruns the content column and clips cards) and never registered the gallery nav-link, so it fails no_horizontal_overflow, visual_regression, and the cross-page dom_assertions while still passing the interaction gate because its filter wiring is correct. The bad solution is a smart-wrong gallery whose filter click flips the active tab but leaves the count frozen at 'Showing 6 of 6 . All patterns' and never filters the grid, whose CSS shingles the cards into an overlapping pile with near-white-on-near-white illegible tabs, and which also omits the nav-link, so it fails all four gates. The offline infrastructure (removing the remote Facebook JSSDK script and remote S3 fork-me ribbon image, and the shared nav-links registry, site-nav renderer, gallery.html markup and site.css design system) is identical across all three legs and is declared, not part of the graded content. The docs home has an inherent CodeMirror-driven mobile-width overflow present identically in all three legs, so the responsive no_horizontal_overflow gate is scoped to the new gallery page states where the reference is a true zero-overflow layout.
